title: UW Rollup Aggregates 1.0
description: The `portfolio_rollup` section payload: aggregate figures a composite states over its children, recomputed by an RFC 0016 receipt verifier (UW Receipt 1.0 §11, RFC 0021 §6). The `fn` vocabulary is fixed, closed, and non-extensible — nothing here lets a module or document author introduce a new aggregation, and nothing here makes the Tier-3 calc engine iterate. A verified rollup means the stated total follows deterministically from those child records as they stand; it does not mean the children are complete, that the portfolio holds every asset it should, or that the members named are the right members.

aggregates.description: The stated aggregates. Each is recomputed independently against exactly the members it names.

id.description: Identity of this aggregate within the section, e.g. `portfolio_noi`.

fn.description: The aggregation applied. Fixed and non-extensible: this is a verifier vocabulary, not an extension of the calc expression language.

over.description: Field path read from each member record, e.g. `noi_model.net_operating_income`. A member whose value at this path cannot be read is unevaluable, never zero — summing what is present would report a confident total over a portfolio the verifier never saw.

members.description: Exactly the members this aggregate covers. A member named twice is refused: it would inflate a sum, and a portfolio total is precisely the figure nobody re-checks by hand.

value.description: The stated result. A verifier recomputes `fn` over the named members and compares; disagreement is `COMP-ROLLUP-DISAGREES` and the receipt is `failed`, decided only after every child's own receipt has been checked.

weight_by.description: Field path supplying weights. REQUIRED for `weighted_average` and MUST NOT appear otherwise. Weights summing to zero is `failed` rather than `unverifiable`: the verifier holds every value it needs, so the stated average is an assertion that cannot be well-defined — a defect in the record, not a gap in the verifier.
